description: 12 tasks performed via the server-rendered multi-page UI only: navigate, read_page/screenshot, click, form_input. No direct API calls.

T1.notes: 1 click failed on render timing, retried. Correct: Sourdough Baking Basics, $35.

T3.notes: Had to scan all 10 checkboxes and find the submit button in a second pass. Correct: Classical Guitar Recital ($18) cheaper.

T4.notes: 1 click failed on render timing, retried. Booking #1 correct.

T5.notes: Navigate to /bookings, fill name-lookup form, re-read page to find the now-rendered inline form, submit. 2 render-timing click failures.

T6.notes: Cheapest task: Cancel button already on-screen from T5's result.

T7.notes: Booking id came back on the confirmation page directly.

T8.notes: 1st attempt (15 seats) returned a bare plain-text error page with no form to retry from ('Booking failed: not enough seats available') -- had to re-navigate to the event page from scratch and refill the whole form to recover. 2nd attempt (10 seats) succeeded as booking #3.

T9.notes: 1st cancel succeeded. The 2nd cancel-attempt sub-task could not be performed as designed: once a booking is cancelled, the DOM template stops rendering its Cancel button entirely (confirmed via find(), 0 matches). The UI prevents the invalid action proactively instead of letting the agent attempt it and fail. Correct answer becomes 'the interface does not expose a way to attempt this,' which is a different (and arguably harder-to-report) outcome than a reactive error.

T10.notes: Same guard as T9: the Update form is also hidden once status != 'confirmed' (confirmed via find(), 0 matches for 'Update'). Task is structurally unreachable through the DOM UI's own affordances.

T11.notes: 1st attempt (1 checkbox) correctly showed 'Select at least two events to compare.' 2nd attempt (2 checkboxes) succeeded: Improv for Beginners ($20) cheaper than Intro to Woodworking ($60).
